own_solution.law: Long-solenoid inductance L = mu0 N^2 pi r^2 / l; steady current I = emf/R1 (the zero-resistance winding shorts the second resistor); all stored energy (1/2) L I^2 is dissipated in the second resistor after the switch opens
assumptions: winding resistance negligible, so the second resistor carries no steady current and receives all of the stored energy

notes: L = 1.257e-6*800^2*pi*(0.015)^2/0.40 = 1.42163e-3 H. I = 12/4 = 3 A; E = 0.5*1.42163e-3*9 = 6.3974e-3 J. With 7.5 V added in series (19.5 V): I = 4.875 A; E = 0.5*1.42163e-3*23.7656 = 0.016893 J. The second resistor's value sets the decay time but not the total energy dissipated in it (C): it enters L di/dt = -R2 i and the integral of R2 i^2 dt = (1/2) L I^2 independent of R2. Doorbell-cell batteries (T200B, TC1E1) are a separate circuit (D). Earlier-run batteries (T212D, T8F98) leave no state (D). T212D and TC1E1 state no number ('modest emf').
